chung.Description:
- Upon finishing the course, students can know the methods to research academic topics such as how to analyze data sets, how to collect the data... so that students can do a research project by themselves.

- "Quantitative Methods" course will cover the fundamental principles of science, some history and philosophy of science, research designs, measurement, sampling and ethics. The course is comparable to a university level introductory course on quantitative research methods in the social sciences, but has a strong focus on research integrity. We will use examples from sociology, political sciences, educational sciences, communication sciences and psychology.

- In "Qualitaty Research Methods" course you will be introduced to the basic ideas behind the qualitative research in social science. You will learn about data collection, description, analysis and interpretation in qualitative research. Qualitative research often involves an iterative process. We will focus on the ingredients required for this process: data collection and analysis. You won't learn how to use qualitative methods by just watching video's, so we put much stress on collecting data through observation and interviewing and on analysing and interpreting the collected data in other assignments.

Obviously, the most important concepts in qualitative research will be discussed, just as we will discuss quality criteria, good practices, ethics, writing some methods of analysis, and mixing methods.

MOO 05: Methods and Statistics in Social Science - Final Research Project
clo: After completing this course, students will be able to: identify some history and philosophy of science, and practice the research designs, measurement, sampling and ethics.
After completing this course, students will be able to: practice data collection, description, analysis and interpretation in qualitative research
After completing this course, students will be able to: know the basics of statistics; not just how to calculate them, but also how to evaluate them.
After completing this course, students will be able to: practice inferential statistics are concerned with making inferences based on relations found in the sample, to relations in the population.

In this capstone project, students will: formulate a research hypothesis and design, come up with operationalizations, create manipulation and measurement instruments, collect data, perform statistical analyses and document the results.
Recognize the inportant of the Course Scientific Research Methods, active learning
